summary: The run built a reasonably strong and compact Act 1 deck, but reached the Slime Boss without potions and then drifted into a low-HP state while several enemies remained alive. The clearest combat issue was spending energy on additional defense when damage was still available, though exact incoming damage is not logged. A secondary preparation issue was spending nearly all remaining gold on Feed immediately before the boss instead of retaining access to a potion option.

lessons.title: Do not add block automatically when damage can prevent future attacks
lessons.situation: When HP is declining, current block is already substantial, and the remaining energy can either add more block or damage an enemy.
lessons.lesson: First assess whether the existing block is likely to cover the attack; if not, prefer legal damage such as Rampage to reduce enemy count or shorten the fight rather than spending the last energy on marginal additional block.
evidence_points: On Turn 8, after Shrug It Off and True Grit, the player had 11 block and 1 energy, with both Defend and Rampage legal, but chose Defend.
The next logged state was Turn 9 at 19/80 HP with Spike Slime at 49 HP and two Acid Slimes still present.
On Turn 11, the player reached 2/80 HP while two enemies remained, then died in the same boss combat.
lessons.reasoning: The log does not provide exact incoming damage, so the precise counterfactual is uncertain. However, the decision clearly exchanged the final energy for more block while a playable attack remained, and the following state shows the fight continued with severe HP loss and multiple enemies alive.

lessons.title: Preserve boss-combat resources when the boss is immediately ahead
lessons.situation: At a late shop before the Act boss, especially when no potion is currently held and the next campfire cannot restore consumables.
lessons.lesson: Treat an immediately usable defensive potion or retained gold as a serious alternative to buying a nonessential card; do not spend almost all gold unless the purchase clearly improves the upcoming boss fight.
evidence_points: At Floor 14, with the Slime Boss next, the player had 78 gold and bought Feed for 71, leaving 7 gold.
That shop offered both a Weak Potion and a Block Potion as alternatives.
The final build lists no potions, and the boss combat began after resting at only 64/80 HP.
lessons.reasoning: The trajectory cannot prove that a potion would have changed the result, and Feed can be valuable. Still, the combination of no potion reserve, incomplete boss-entry HP, and nearly all gold spent on a card makes consumable preservation a meaningful preparation heuristic.

lessons.title: Repeat early deck thinning plus high-impact picks
lessons.situation: During Act 1, when offered a card removal or a strong card that immediately improves damage, scaling, or defense.
lessons.lesson: Continue prioritizing early removal of starter Strikes and high-impact cards over low-value filler; the goal is a compact deck whose draws reliably contain meaningful attacks and defensive tools.
evidence_points: The Neow sequence selected Strike twice for removal, and the Floor 5 shop removed another Strike.
The run selected strong early additions including Carnage, Rampage, True Grit, Shrug It Off, Impervious, and Ghostly Armor.
The final build contained 18 cards and included Carnage, Rampage, Impervious, Ghostly Armor, Shrug It Off, and Dropkick.
lessons.reasoning: These choices produced a relatively compact deck with multiple high-impact cards rather than a heavily diluted starter deck. This strategy is worth retaining, while future runs should pair it with better boss-fight resource and combat sequencing.
